pos.personaBrief: Dynamo valued possession but sat deep and countered Bayern 1975 and used quick forwards for counters (1988, 1997); he adapted by match, so possession is a tool, not a dogma.

pro.personaBrief: Quick counters with two fast playmaking forwards, long balls over the line from defenders (1988) and long balls to forwards (1997), few-touch transitions.

est.personaBrief: Universality and interchangeability, fluid systems hard to label (1975), yet rehearsed roles and collective understanding of a scientific system.

lar.personaBrief: Field enlarged in possession with full-backs and wingers providing width (1988), but 4-3-1-2 in 1986 with conservative full-backs and central focus.

blo.personaBrief: Intense pressing for 90 minutes, immediate counterpress in the final third, forwards defending from the half line, pressing at home; dropped deep only for specific opponents.

mar.personaBrief: Man-coverage on Gullit and man-orientations with zonal cover; adjusted to zonal when lines were broken.

pla.personaBrief: Studied the opponent to find counter-play and changed formation per match (Netherlands, Ireland 1988, Bayern 1975), though with a firm underlying method.

res.personaBrief: Games fade but results stay; pragmatic, held the ball when ahead, sat deep in Europe when a result was needed.

sis.personaBrief: System over individuality; Ballon d'Or forwards subordinated to the collective, a strict ensemble of believers.

jog.personaBrief: Emphasised fitness and intense 90-minute pressing, universal players; but also technical, passing players like Zavarov and Shevchenko.

bas.personaBrief: Nurtured homegrown talent (Beszonov, Baltacha, Mykhaylychenko) alongside signings, results first; sold Shevchenko and Rebrov.

lid.personaBrief: Intense, fierce, strict disciplinarian controlling every aspect of players' lives; the sergeant major.
